## Why a Budget Build in 2026  
Gaming hardware keeps getting cheaper while performance climbs. In 2026, a solid 1080p‑60 fps experience is achievable for under $800 if you pick the right parts. Building your own rig lets you avoid markup, upgrade later, and learn valuable troubleshooting skills. Plus, the DIY community offers endless guides and deals that make the process fun rather than intimidating.

## Core Parts for Budget Build  
A gaming PC hinges on five key components: CPU, GPU, motherboard, RAM, and storage. Power supply, case, and cooling round out the list. Each piece must balance price and capability, especially when you’re targeting a tight budget.

### Choosing the Right CPU  
For 2026, AMD’s Ryzen 5 7600X and Intel’s Core i5‑13400F remain the sweet spots. Both deliver six cores and strong single‑thread performance, crucial for most games. Look for sales on the previous generation (Ryzen 5 5600X or i5‑12400F) if you need to shave $20‑$30 off the price.

### GPU Options Under $200  
The graphics card is the biggest performance lever. In the budget tier, NVIDIA’s RTX 4060 8 GB and AMD’s RX 7600 8 GB trade blows around $180‑$220. If you can stretch to $250, the RTX 4060 Ti offers noticeable ray‑tracing gains without breaking the bank. Keep an eye on refurbished or open‑box deals—they often shave $30‑$50 off MSRP.

### Motherboard & RAM Basics  
A B650 (AMD) or B760 (Intel) motherboard gives you PCIe 4.0 slots, decent VRMs, and future‑upgrade paths for under $100. Pair it with 16 GB (2×8 GB) of DDR5‑5600 RAM; prices have dropped to roughly $55‑$65 for a reliable kit. If DDR5 still feels steep, a DDR4‑3200 kit on a B660/B760 board saves about $20 while losing only a few percent in bandwidth.

### Storage Choices for Speed  
An NVMe SSD is now the standard for fast load times. A 500 GB PCIe 4.0 drive costs around $40‑$50, while a 1 TB model sits near $70. If you need extra space for a game library, add a cheap 2 TB SATA SSD or HDD for $45‑$60. The OS and your favorite titles should live on the NVMe drive for snappy responsiveness.
